source.title: Learning Sparse Neural Networks for Better Generalization

record.file_problem: Full text is present. It is a doctoral consortium research overview, not a detailed experimental report.
record.tranche_reason: Summarizes empirical findings on sparse MLPs and RNNs, extending the generalization discussion to sparse architectures; it reports no test of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The text reports qualitative outcomes from the authors’ prior work and a sharpness observation. It gives no experimental tables or numerical results for these findings.
record.test_reason: The overview reports sparse-versus-dense performance and reduced sharpness, but none measures a listed claim version. It provides no convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, width sweep, optimizer comparison, or sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author summarizes empirical advantages of sparse networks while stating that their mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Landscape changes enabling escape from local optima or saddle points are conjectured; generalization guarantees remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: The text summarizes sparse-network approaches and prior empirical findings, not a comparison of the original claim’s methods. It does not report random-label fitting or the listed interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse RNNs reportedly outperform dense RNNs, and Selfish-RNNs improve language modeling performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some sparse RNN methods improve predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Intrinsically sparse MLPs reportedly generalize better than fully connected counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive sparse connectivity can improve MLP generalization relative to dense connectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: High sparsity reportedly reduces minimizer sharpness, without a measured relationship to generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High sparsity can reduce neural-network minimizer sharpness.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-20), Doctoral Consortium Track
record.problems: The reported empirical findings are qualitative summaries without datasets, numerical results, uncertainty, or detailed methods. Several are attributed to the authors’ earlier work. The sharpness statement does not specify a measure or establish a relation to the training-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results on test accuracy for the sparse MLPs or on network topology similarity are given beyond qualitative descriptions; the topology-similarity method is not reported as a result bearing on the claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects across data sizes and configurations, including removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no numerical experimental tables. Row states indicate that the measures cannot determine any listed version; they do not deny the qualitative sparse-network findings. R1 and R3 should be treated as summaries of earlier publications, not independent experimental results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD under different tuning regimes.
Large-batch training and changes to the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
